automation.body: The English Vocabulary Daily channel posts on a fixed schedule — one word at 07:15 UTC and one quiz at 17:15 UTC — driven by a GitHub Actions cron job. The workflow picks the lesson from the day of the year, so the same date always produces the same lesson, and the post goes out with no AI at runtime and no one pressing a button. What you see on this page is the live state of that system, read from the public repo.
automation.deterministic: No AI at runtime — the same code picks the same lesson for the same day, every day.

how.heading: How I work

steps.body: Every project lives in a public GitHub repo from the start, with its code, its lesson bank, and its workflow files visible. If it is not in the repo, it is not part of the project.
steps.title: Build in public

steps.body: Where a task repeats on a schedule, it runs on GitHub Actions — not on a server I have to maintain, and not by hand. The vocabulary channel posts twice a day because a cron job posts it, not because someone remembers to.
steps.title: Automate the repeatable part

steps.body: Tokens and chat IDs go in GitHub Secrets, never in a commit. The code is MIT-licensed and the lesson bank is CC BY 4.0, so anyone can read, check, or reuse the work — without ever seeing a credential.
steps.title: Keep secrets out of the code
